title: X Feed Digest
summary: Gemini’s Deep Think upgrade and Veo 3.1 multi‑image prompts led the product news, while Cloudflare’s HTML→Markdown edge conversion points to cheaper agent browsing.
Commentary on GPT‑5.3 rollout dynamics, NVIDIA’s voice‑AI stack compression, and OpenClaw workflow tips stressed performance vs. scale and practical ops.
AI policy/business tensions surfaced in the Pentagon–Anthropic debate and Dario Amodei interview takeaways on compute spend and timelines.
Markets focus included Duolingo’s valuation gap, a macro‑heavy week (GDP/PCE, key earnings), and a warning about a K‑shaped AI labor market.

items.title: @AlchainHust: Dario Amodei interview takeaways
items.body: A long recap of Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei’s podcast hit on revenue growth, cautious compute spending, and a sober view that AI coding gains are still limited. He also sketched near‑term timelines for ‘data‑center geniuses’ and backed federal standards plus chip export controls.

items.title: @GeminiApp: Gemini 3 Deep Think upgrade
items.body: Google rolled out a major Deep Think upgrade aimed at practical reasoning tasks, including turning sketches into 3D‑printable models and modeling physical systems in code. It’s rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers via the tools menu.

items.title: @GeminiApp: Veo 3.1 multi‑image prompts
items.body: Veo 3.1 now lets you attach multiple reference images to video prompts, giving more control over hard‑to‑describe scenes and styles. The thread shows how swapping images changes the output.

items.title: @xiaohu: Cloudflare HTML→Markdown for agents
items.body: Cloudflare added an edge feature that returns Markdown when agents request pages with “Accept: text/markdown,” cutting token usage dramatically. It converts HTML at the CDN edge and sends the lighter Markdown back.

items.title: @BensonTWN: GPT‑5.3 hype caveat
items.body: A reminder that GPT‑5.3 impressions are from a small Codex‑only rollout, where compute is plentiful and latency is lower. The author argues real‑world performance could shift once it scales to full API and ChatGPT traffic.

items.title: @aakashgupta: Voice‑AI costs compressing
items.body: NVIDIA’s open‑weights PersonaPlex (single 7B model) is framed as collapsing the ASR→LLM→TTS stack into one model with low latency. The claim: this could commoditize per‑minute voice‑agent APIs and slash costs.

items.title: @xxx111god: Claude Code + OpenClaw workflow tips
items.body: Practical workflow notes: prefer sub‑agent spawns over worktrees, require planning before complex changes, and keep a lightweight post‑mortem log of mistakes. Also a strong permissions model—read freely, ask before writes, confirm deletes.

items.title: @kimmonismus: Pentagon–Anthropic tensions
items.body: The post claims the Pentagon may reconsider Anthropic partnerships after the company refused “all lawful purposes” use, citing bans on mass surveillance and fully autonomous weapons. It frames a broader clash between safety limits and defense demands.

items.title: @aakashgupta: Duolingo fundamentals vs price
items.body: Duolingo shares are ~70% off the 2025 highs despite strong revenue growth and improving margins. The thread points to bookings deceleration and tougher comps as likely drivers behind the market’s re‑rating.

items.title: @swangentr: This week’s macro catalysts
items.body: A calendar‑style outlook flags Q4 GDP and the Fed‑watched PCE report on Friday, a potential Supreme Court tariffs decision, and earnings from Walmart and John Deere among the highlights.

items.title: @milesdeutscher: The K‑shaped AI economy
items.body: An argument that AI skills are already creating a K‑shaped split—high earners who leverage AI vs. workers who are managed by it. The post cites wage premiums for AI‑skilled workers and urges action in the next 2–3 years.

items.title: @elormkdaniel: Laptop battery reality check
items.body: Keeping a lithium‑ion laptop plugged in isn’t instantly harmful, but sitting at 100% charge—especially with heat—degrades health over time. The suggestion: use an 80% charge limit when mostly plugged in.

items.title: @elormkdaniel: Why VLC stays free
items.body: A breakdown of VLC’s growth loop: it’s free, works on odd formats, and spreads via word‑of‑mouth, which would be undermined by monetization. The claim is that staying free is central to its distribution moat.
